content:
The Bahrain Grand Prix will be broadcast live for free on Apple TV this weekend, with no subscription required. Quite interestingly, the Bahrain Grand Prix is actually held at Sepang, Malaysia.

Normally you need a paid subscription to watch F1 on Apple TV, but this weekend anyone can watch for free. You can catch up on the qualifying replay first, and then tune in for the live race in the early hours of this morning, with the race starting at 3 AM Eastern Time.

All you need to do is install the Apple TV app on a supported device, be in the US, and stay up late to watch the live broadcast.

Coverage begins at 1:50 AM Eastern Time, with the race scheduled to start at 3 AM. Of course, if you'd rather get some sleep, you can also watch it on demand later at your own pace.

The Apple TV app can be installed on Apple devices, Amazon Fire Stick, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox, Android, and more, and you can also watch via the browser at tv.apple.com.

Qualifying has already been completed earlier, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen taking the first pole position of the season, Lewis Hamilton in second, and championship leader Kim Antonelli in third. This is Red Bull's most promising chance of winning a race so far this season.

You may be wondering why the Bahrain Grand Prix is being held in Malaysia. Normally, the Bahrain round would have taken place at the start of the season, but due to the ongoing war in Iran, the race was cancelled, and the Bahrain organisers decided to sponsor a race held elsewhere in the world.

Although Sepang is no longer on the official F1 calendar, it has always been one of the fans' favourite circuits and should deliver an exciting and thrilling race.

Just a reminder — you can watch it for free via the Apple TV app, with no subscription required. The race starts at 3 AM Eastern Time, with live coverage beginning at 1:50 AM.
